dem_viewshed — DEM visibility op

• Data kinds: depth → image2d

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.dem_viewshed(dem, cell_size, observer_rc, observer_height_m=1.7, target_height_m=0.0, max_distance_m=None) (to call the implementation directly, import demops; demops.dem_viewshed(dem, cell_size, observer_rc, observer_height_m=1.7, target_height_m=0.0, max_distance_m=None); from the registry, opsdem.get("dem_viewshed"))

Usage

Visible area from 1 point (1 = visible). Decides whether the line of sight is blocked by the terrain.

observer_rc is (row, col). The observer itself is always visible.

Procedure: eye height eye = z[observer] + observer_height_m. The line of sight to each cell is divided into ceil(hypot(H, W)) equal parts, and if at any intermediate cell the terrain elevation angle (z_mid - eye) / d_mid exceeds the target elevation angle (z + target_height_m - eye) / d, the cell is occluded (0). Intermediate points are rounded to the nearest cell, so oblique lines of sight include grid error. Earth curvature and atmospheric refraction are not included (beyond a few km, correct separately).

• dem: (H, W) [m], 3x3 or larger, sentinel values rejected (same contract as dem_slope). nan cells make comparisons false, so they neither occlude nor get occluded and stay at 1.

• cell_size: [m], positive. Used for distance tests.

• observer_rc: integer (row, col) within the grid. Outside or not a pair gives ValueError.

• observer_height_m / target_height_m: height above ground [m]. Defaults are eye height 1.7 m and ground surface 0 m. For the viewshed from a steel tower, raise observer_height_m.

• max_distance_m: cells farther than this are 0 (unlimited if omitted).

• Returns: (H, W) float64 of 1 / 0. The observer is always 1.

• Cost: whole grid × ceil(hypot(H, W)) vector operations.

dem_horizon_angle / dem_sky_view_factor conversely give "how much sky is visible from each cell".
